questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the result of `[] + {}` in JavaScript?

options.A: "[object Object]"

questions.explanation: Array [] converts to empty string ''; object {} converts to '[object Object]'; string concatenation yields '[object Object]'.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the result of `{}` in statement context followed by `+ []` -> `{} + []` evaluated as expression in JS console?
questions.explanation: In statement context, `{}` is parsed as an empty block statement; `+ []` coerces empty array to number 0.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What does `true + false` evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Numeric addition coerces boolean true -> 1 and false -> 0, yielding 1 + 0 = 1.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the result of `NaN === NaN` in JavaScript?

options.A: false

questions.explanation: In JavaScript, IEEE 754 standard defines NaN as non-equal to everything, including itself (NaN === NaN is false).

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: How can you accurately check if a variable `x` is strictly `NaN`?

options.A: Number.isNaN(x)

questions.explanation: Number.isNaN(x) checks if x is type Number and value NaN without false positives from global isNaN coercion.

questions.question: What happens when accessing a property on an object that exists neither on the object nor anywhere on its prototype chain?

options.A: Returns undefined

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question:
What is the output of this code?
```js
Promise.resolve(1)
  .then(x => x + 1)
  .then(x => { throw new Error('My Error'); })
  .catch(() => 100)
  .then(x => console.log(x));
```
questions.explanation: The thrown error bypasses subsequent thens and hits `.catch()`, which returns resolved 100 passed to next `.then()`.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: Which technique optimizes recursive calls in supporting engines to prevent call stack growth?

options.A: Proper Tail Call (PTC) optimization

questions.explanation: Tail Call Optimization reuses current stack frame if recursive call is in tail position.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is function currying in JavaScript?

options.A: Transforming a function with multiple arguments into a sequence of functions each taking a single argument

questions.explanation: Currying translates `f(a, b, c)` into callable chain `f(a)(b)(c)`.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: Why are keys in a `WeakMap` NOT enumerable via methods like `Object.keys()`?

options.A: Non-enumerability prevents non-deterministic behavior caused by unpredictable garbage collector runs

questions.explanation: Exposing WeakMap keys would introduce non-determinism based on when GC sweeps collect unreferenced objects.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: Are exported variables in ES Modules live bindings or static value copies?

options.A: Live bindings (importers see real-time value updates made inside exporting module)

questions.explanation: ES module exports are live bindings; mutations inside the source module are reflected across all importing modules.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: Which prefix syntax designates a private class field/method in modern ES2022 JavaScript?

options.A: # (hash prefix e.g. #privateField)

questions.explanation: The `#` prefix creates hard private class fields inaccessible outside the class body.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.topic: Deep cloning and Structured Clone API
questions.question: Which native modern JavaScript method creates a deep clone of a complex object containing nested objects, dates, and arrays?

options.A: structuredClone(obj)

questions.explanation: structuredClone() creates deep copies of structured data including cyclic references, ArrayBuffers, Dates, and Maps.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: Which type of value CANNOT be cloned using `structuredClone()`?

options.A: Functions and DOM elements

questions.explanation: structuredClone() throws DataCloneError if attempting to clone Functions or DOM nodes.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: When an object has `[Symbol.toPrimitive](hint)` defined, what hints can JavaScript pass to this method during coercion?

options.A: 'number', 'string', or 'default'

questions.explanation: The JS coercion engine passes string hints 'number', 'string', or 'default'.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the key difference between `Promise.any()` and `Promise.race()`?

options.A: `Promise.any()` ignores rejections and resolves with first FULFILLED promise; `Promise.race()` settles on first promise to settle (fulfill OR reject)

questions.explanation: Promise.any fulfills on first fulfillment (rejecting with AggregateError if all reject); Promise.race settles on first settled item.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: When does `Promise.any()` reject with an `AggregateError`?

options.A: When ALL promises in the input iterable reject

questions.explanation: Promise.any() throws AggregateError wrapping individual rejection reasons when every input promise fails.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: In node/browser environments, what happens if a microtask recursively queues another microtask infinitely?

options.A: The microtask queue starves the Macrotask queue, freezing I/O and UI rendering indefinitely
options.B: The event loop skips microtasks and runs Macrotasks
options.C: Engine throws Stack Overflow error instantly

questions.explanation: Microtask queue must drain completely before event loop moves on; recursive microtasks block rendering and macrotask execution.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is a primary difference between JavaScript `Set` and `Map`/`Object`?

options.A: `Set` stores unique values of any type with no key-value pairing

questions.explanation: Set is a collection of unique values without distinct keys.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What occurs when executing `class MyArray extends Array {}` and calling `new MyArray().slice()` in ES6?

options.A: Returns an instance of `MyArray` (using Symbol.species)

questions.explanation: Built-in array methods like slice use `[Symbol.species]` to instantiate derived class `MyArray` objects.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is `globalThis` in modern ECMAScript?

options.A: A standardized universal global object reference available across browser window, Web Workers, and Node.js environments

questions.explanation: globalThis provides a unified standard property for accessing global scope across any JavaScript execution platform.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: How do you attach an underlying cause error when re-throwing an error in ES2022?

options.A: throw new Error('Failed operation', { cause: originalError });

questions.explanation: ES2022 introduced options object `{ cause: err }` parameter to Error constructors for chained error diagnostics.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What does `[10, 20, 30].at(-1)` return in modern JavaScript?
questions.explanation: .at(index) accepts negative integers to count back from the last item (-1 returns last item 30).

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: Where is top-level `await` allowed without wrapping inside an `async` function in modern JS?

options.A: At the top level of ES Modules (.mjs / type="module")
options.C: Inside standard HTML inline event handlers

questions.explanation: Top-level await is valid at top level of ES modules.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the result of `Object.is(-0, +0)` compared to `-0 === +0`?

options.A: `Object.is(-0, +0)` is false; `-0 === +0` is true

questions.explanation: Object.is differentiates -0 and +0 (returns false), whereas strict equality === treats them as equal (returns true).

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is a 'trap' in JavaScript Proxy objects?

options.A: A method that intercepts and customizes internal object operations (e.g., get, set, deleteProperty)

questions.explanation: Proxy traps intercept low-level object target operations.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: How do you create a Proxy that can be turned off/disabled later?

options.A: Proxy.revocable(target, handler)

questions.explanation: Proxy.revocable returns object `{ proxy, revoke }` allowing invocation of `revoke()` to disable proxy access.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the purpose of the `Atomics` object in multi-threaded JavaScript (Web Workers)?

options.A: Provides atomic operations for shared memory across threads to prevent race conditions

questions.explanation: Atomics ensures memory operations on SharedArrayBuffer instances occur predictably without thread race collisions.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What does `.toString()` return on a function in modern ES2019+?

options.A: Exact source code text representation including comments and whitespace

questions.explanation: ES2019 updated `Function.prototype.toString()` to return exact source code slice including white-space and comments.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the result of `'5'.padStart(3, '0')`?
questions.explanation: padStart(targetLength, padString) pads current string from start until target length 3 is met ('005').

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: How do you declare a `BigInt` primitive literal representing arbitrary precision integers?
questions.explanation: Appending trailing `n` to an integer literal constructs a BigInt primitive.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What happens when performing `10n + 5` (mixing BigInt and Number)?

options.A: Throws TypeError

questions.explanation: JavaScript forbids mixing BigInt and Number types implicitly in arithmetic operations, throwing TypeError.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What does `x ||= y` do in ES2021?

options.A: Assigns `y` to `x` ONLY IF `x` is falsy (`x || (x = y)`)
options.B: Assigns y to x only if x is nullish

questions.explanation: Logical OR assignment `x ||= y` assigns y to x if x evaluates to falsy.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What does `x ??= y` do in ES2021?

options.A: Assigns `y` to `x` ONLY IF `x` is nullish (null or undefined)
options.B: Assigns y to x if x is false
options.C: Assigns y to x if x is 0

questions.explanation: Nullish logical assignment `x ??= y` assigns y to x only if x is null or undefined.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the purpose of `WeakRef` introduced in ES2021?

options.A: Holds a weak reference to a target object without preventing that target object from being garbage collected

questions.explanation: WeakRef lets developers hold weak object references that don't protect target objects from GC removal.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What is the purpose of `FinalizationRegistry` in ES2021?

options.A: Allows registering a cleanup callback triggered after a target object has been garbage collected

questions.explanation: FinalizationRegistry provides callbacks notifying when registered objects get swept by garbage collector.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: What does `Object.groupBy(array, callback)` return in modern ES2024 JavaScript?

options.A: An object with null-prototype containing properties grouping array items by callback string return keys

questions.explanation: Object.groupBy groups items into an object whose keys are returned from the group criteria callback.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.topic: RegExp v flag and set notation
questions.question: What feature does the RegExp `v` flag (UnicodeSets) enable in modern JS?

options.A: Enables set operations (intersection, subtraction) inside character classes in regular expressions

questions.explanation: The `v` flag extends regex character classes to support set difference, intersection, and nested classes.

questions.subject: JavaScript
questions.question: Why is the modern `Temporal` API replacing legacy `Date` object in JavaScript?

options.A: Provides immutable date-time objects, handles timezones explicitly, and eliminates zero-based month bugs
options.C: Date object is deprecated in Node

questions.explanation: Temporal provides a robust modern specification for date/time computations, overcoming Date's mutability and timezone pitfalls.
